# Native Moco Initial-State Bindings

## Status and Scope

This provisional F07/F08 pathway is scoped by child #11949 under parent #11791 and the full feedback
control epic #11784. It fixes an executable Moco initialization boundary and
records genuine synthetic optimization followed by independent native muscle
replay. It does not close production model, physiology, capture, contact/grip,
complete native state, six-engine parity, or manual publication gates.

`tour_matching.MocoInitialBindings` supplies immutable caller-declared state
bounds, fixed initial continuous state, and scalar actuator-control bounds to
`build_moco_study(..., initial_bindings=bindings)`. The builder applies them
before `initCasADiSolver()` and `createGuess()`. Previously, a compliant muscle's
`/fiber_length` state had no bound information when guess creation occurred;
the native failure is retained with the evidence. Guess values are numerical
seeds, not initial-state constraints.

The optional argument preserves existing exploratory callers. Supplying no
bindings does not create a complete initialization or qualification claim.
The binding object is not arbitrary SimTK state serialization. The independent
replay admission and evidence limits in the native muscle replay and experiment
bundle chapters remain authoritative.

## Contract and Equations

For exact native continuous-state names $s_i$, caller intervals $[l_i,u_i]$ and
frozen values $x_{i,0}$, the binding enforces

$$l_i\le x_i(t)\le u_i,\qquad x_i(t_0)=x_{i,0},\qquad
l_i\le x_{i,0}\le u_i.$$

State-bound and initial-value names must match each other and the unchanged
initialized model's named continuous states. Control bounds must cover the
actual native scalar actuator paths. Values must be finite real numbers;
booleans, reversed intervals, unknown/missing paths and initial values outside
bounds fail. Fixed-width bounds are permitted. Source maps are copied and
exposed read-only. No physiological bounds are invented from suffixes in the API.

Existing controllers and `PositionMotion` require a separate binding policy and
are rejected recursively before native initialization. Multi-control actuators
are unsupported. This is not a general inventory of Moco Input-controller
variables, registered discrete state, modeling options, locks, constraints or
plugin state. Caller bounds cannot qualify those mechanisms. Native model
initialization discovers names without equilibrating supplied initial values,
adding reserves, processing anatomy, or changing muscle laws.

The experiment minimizes marker tracking and control effort over $[0,.1]$ s:

$$J=w_m\int\|p(x(t))-p_{\rm ref}(t)\|^2\,dt
+w_u\int u(t)^2\,dt,$$

with $w_m=1$ and $w_u=10^{-8}$. Here $p_{\rm ref}$ is Moco's spline reference
constructed from the written TRC, not the linear diagnostic reference used below.
The weights are experiment choices, not physiological acceptance limits.

## Actual Native Fixture and Numerical Policy

The unchanged native fixture has a 1 kg body, one SliderJoint, zero gravity,
one `Millard2012EquilibriumMuscle`, fixed path points and a marker at the moving
body origin. Nominal maximum isometric force is 10 N, optimal fiber length .1 m,
tendon slack length .2 m and pennation zero. It contains no reserve/assistance
actuator, contact force, or capture data. The marker's world x position equals
the slider coordinate for this fixture only.

The prepared four-state initial condition is slider position .31 m, speed zero,
activation .05 and compliant fiber length .108573946282611 m. Initial muscle
equilibration occurs once during fixture preparation, before export/freeze; it
is not rerun after replay restoration. Explicit experiment bounds are position
[.2,.4] m, speed [-2,2] m/s, activation [.001,1], fiber length [.05,.2] m and
excitation [.001,1]. These are synthetic numerical bounds, not donor-derived
physiological limits.

The teacher is native forward dynamics under $u(t)=.3+2t$, sampled at 21 times
with 200 Hz TRC metadata. A constant initial-state trajectory seeds Moco. Actual
OpenSim 4.6, CasADi/IPOPT, one solver worker and 10/20/40/80 mesh intervals were used;
optimization convergence and constraint tolerances were $10^{-7}$, with at most
60 iterations. The executed SDK's Hermite-Simpson/explicit-dynamics defaults and
linear control-interior-point policy were reviewed. The final receipts record
the explicitly set solver options; do not infer a fully serialized solver
configuration from those fields alone.

The existing F06 muscle bundle replays the optimized excitation with a fresh
native model and the frozen initial state, with no access to marker observations,
feedback or state resets. Its native input is piecewise linear in physical time.
Default replay integration accuracy is $10^{-8}$; an independent accuracy
$10^{-10}$ run checks integration sensitivity. Before F06 replay, the actual T01
bundle is serialized, saved as `native_replay_bundle.json`, and reloaded through
the Tools authority. The output-grid refinement preserves every original control
knot and value exactly and adds 101 requested physical-time probes. The resulting
unions contain 101/121/161/241 samples for 10/20/40/80 intervals. The maximum
control-function difference on 1001 check points is $5.55112\times10^{-17}$.

Scoring uses the same 101 requested probe times for every mesh, selecting a
coincident original knot without retiming it; maximum observed probe-clock
difference is $1.38778\times10^{-17}$ s. Averaging every union sample would
change the scoring weights across meshes and is not the reported metric.
These are output/probe grids, not the adaptive integrator's internal step
sequence or a continuous collocation defect proof.

## Measured Results and Remaining State Disagreement

All four native public-API solves returned `Solve_Succeeded`. Values below
come from the corrected archived `grid-preserving-final-mesh-*` receipts/logs.
They use common 101-point scoring, not the differing union sample counts:

| Quantity | 10 Intervals | 20 Intervals | 40 Intervals | 80 Intervals |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| IPOPT iterations | 25 | 23 | 12 | 12 |
| NLP constraint violation | 5.62008e-8 | 3.52779e-8 | 5.95911e-8 | 9.56112e-9 |
| Maximum variable-bound violation | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Optimized versus replay position maximum, m | 8.02227e-6 | 8.15248e-7 | 2.17795e-8 | 1.20421e-7 |
| Optimized versus replay speed maximum, m/s | 1.70995e-4 | 2.46326e-5 | 3.62531e-6 | 1.57986e-6 |
| Optimized versus replay activation maximum | .00723379 | .00189424 | .000589070 | .0000929729 |
| Optimized versus replay fiber-length maximum, m | 6.38536e-5 | 1.73917e-5 | 4.55531e-6 | 1.07075e-6 |
| Common-probe replay marker RMSE versus native teacher, m | 6.24609e-6 | 2.91968e-6 | 3.39637e-6 | 3.74765e-6 |
| Common-probe replay RMSE versus linear rounded TRC, m | 8.58593e-6 | 5.18683e-6 | 4.15497e-6 | 4.38346e-6 |
| Repeated native replay full-state maximum difference | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Solve time, s | .5051 | .8373 | .9420 | 1.7031 |
| Total experiment time, s | 1.2267 | 1.5948 | 1.7855 | 2.6203 |

The default-versus-tighter integration activation differences are 4.95820e-8,
6.34056e-8, 6.68852e-9 and 2.50735e-9, much smaller than the corresponding
collocation-versus-native discrepancies. Activation, speed and fiber-length
agreement improve across these refinements, but position error increases from
40 to 80 intervals. Marker RMSE also is not monotone. Four successful solves do
not establish asymptotic convergence, global optimality or a passed full-state
acceptance tolerance. The remaining 80-interval activation discrepancy is
.0000929729; no physiological or numerical threshold is invented after the run.

Recovery of the synthetic teacher is a separate comparison. At .1 s, the
80-interval dense native replay activation is .45835647 while teacher activation
is .47638623, a difference of .01802976. The corresponding 20-interval difference
is .09342181. Neither is the optimized-versus-replay activation error in the
table. The current marker/effort objective has not recovered the teacher's state;
this observation alone does not prove universal structural non-identifiability.

The native-teacher comparison uses separately integrated unrounded truth. The
other diagnostic uses linear interpolation of the six-decimal written TRC.
Neither is Moco's spline tracking objective. Timings describe this local
synthetic process, not fleet throughput or production scaling.

## Superseded Dense Diagnostics

The original `public-mesh-10-final` and `public-mesh-20-final` archives remain
byte-for-byte intact. Their original-grid optimized-versus-native state errors
remain valid. Their dense diagnostic procedure resampled controls on a plain
101-point grid, which omitted some original 20-mesh control knots and could
change the input function. Those dense metrics and related teacher comparisons
are superseded by the corrected four-mesh evidence, even where rounded numbers
are nearly unchanged. The earlier desktop preview binds the old 20-mesh receipt
and must not be relabeled as a corrected run. No historical receipt was rewritten.

## Runtime and Durable Provenance

OpenSim 4.6 and its existing DLLs provide the native evidence. A preceding plugin
search failure is retained. Setting `CASADIPATH` and prepending the existing
OpenSim package directory to the child process `PATH` enabled CasADi/IPOPT
loading; no installation or permanent environment mutation was performed.

The archived final receipts bind the exact executed experiment script, the four
producer/replay source modules, synthetic model/TRC/guess/solution/NPZ artifacts,
and installed native DLL/PYD hashes. Each corrected run also archives the exact
serialized T01 bundle used through the existing source-bound F06 seam; this does
not expand that seam's bounded native-state admission. Historical executed script
bytes remain text evidence, separate from maintained executable source.

See `docs/development/moco_state_binding_11791/DESIGN.md` and `TURNOVER.md` for
reproduction and publication handoff, and the local evidence `MANIFEST.json` for
exact archive hashes. The 31-test actual OpenSim SDK run covers state/general/
control bounds, fixed initial constraints despite a conflicting guess, malformed
maps, controller refusal and a native six-control `BodyActuator` refusal. A
default-runtime skip is not native evidence.

Production anatomy and passive readiness, actual capture attachments and frozen
training calibration, native constraints/contact/grip, full-state admission,
independent full-horizon replay, uncertainty/perturbation validation and all
required six-engine/model variants remain required. Canonical calculation
coverage, generated-document parity and publication approval remain blocked.
